Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test `testPcts()` calls `getPct` passing an `Object`, specifically an `Integer` cast to `Object`. The test expects the percentage of values equal to 3 (or `three`) to be 0.5.

Looking at the implementation of `Frequency.getPct(Object v)`, it is deprecated and internally calls `getCumPct((Comparable<?>) v)`. Calling `getCumPct` returns the cumulative percentage up to the specified value, not the simple percentage of exactly that value. This means that the return value is the cumulative distribution percentage, not the percentage of the exact frequency.

On the other hand, `Frequency.getPct(Comparable<?> v)` correctly returns the percentage of values equal to `v` by dividing the count of `v` by the sum of all frequencies.

The bug originates from the fact that the deprecated `getPct(Object)` implementation uses `getCumPct` (cumulative) instead of `getPct(Comparable<?>)` (exact percentage). Therefore, the test expecting the exact percentage value (0.5) gets an incorrect cumulative percentage result, leading to the failure.

The current bug report highlights this issue, pointing out that all `getPct` calls through `Object` are cumulatively counting instead of directly giving the exact percentage.

No other recent bug reports seem relevant to this specific Frequency getPct issue.

In summary, the root cause is that the deprecated `getPct(Object)` uses the wrong method `getCumPct(Comparable<?>)` internally instead of `getPct(Comparable<?>)` resulting in incorrect behavior for calls passing an `Object` rather than a `Comparable`. The test expects exact percentage but gets cumulative percentage, causing the failure.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
